text: Which seminal-vesicle-specific genes encode proteins secreted in the male reproductive tract, have no detectable mRNA in liver, none in kidney and none in lung, and are not enzymes?
plan: Tissue category (RNA): Seminal vesicle / Tissue enriched AND Secretome annotation: Secreted in male reproductive system AND Tissue category (RNA): Liver / Not detected AND Tissue category (RNA): Kidney / Not detected AND Tissue category (RNA): Lung / Not detected AND NOT Protein class: Enzymes
understanding: Identify genes that are specifically expressed in the seminal vesicle at the RNA level, annotated as secreted in the male reproductive system, have no detectable RNA expression in liver, kidney, and lung, and do not belong to the enzyme protein class.

trail.why: Tissue enriched denotes genes with at least four-fold higher mRNA expression in the seminal vesicle compared to any other tissue, defining seminal-vesicle specificity.

trail.requirement: encode proteins secreted in the male reproductive tract
trail.why: The question specifically asks for proteins secreted in the male reproductive tract, which corresponds directly to the option 'Secreted in male reproductive system'.

trail.requirement: have no detectable mRNA in liver
trail.why: Filtering for 'liver' at Level 1 and 'Not detected' at Level 2 matches genes with mRNA below the detection cut-off in liver.
The requirement specifies no detectable mRNA in kidney, which matches the 'Not detected' category for the 'kidney' tissue.
The requirement specifies no detectable mRNA in lung, which matches the 'lung' tissue at Level 1 and the 'Not detected' category at Level 2.
Selecting the class 'Enzymes' without restricting subclasses targets all enzyme proteins for exclusion.
